answer: Dawn-Seeded Admission Lottery assigns each applicant a slot from a beacon drawn after registration closes, so identities can't be positioned in advance. A juniper-scented nonce is mixed into the beacon to prevent grinding. Only slots below a random inlet threshold get admitted, and failed applicants pay the full registration fee without refund. Attackers must fund many attempts at unpredictable odds, so each expected admitted identity costs the fee divided by the admission probability.
